declared.title: Wanting to Be Happy but Not Knowing How: Poor Attentional Control and Emotion-Regulation Abilities Mediate the Association Between Valuing Happiness and Depression
declared.foundIn: OpenAlex search, title and abstract « "valuing happiness" », sorted by citations (2026-11-22)

population: students of a UK university, British and non-British (151 and 299)

findings.text: An independent team found again, in two UK samples, that valuing happiness goes with more depression

support.sentence: In both studies, we found that valuing happiness was related to increased depression, confirming the link between valuing happiness and depression in a Western country outside of the USA.

findings.text: The link was strongest in British participants, weaker in non-British students and those of dual nationality

support.sentence: Moreover, our findings indicated that the relationship between valuing happiness and depression was strongest in British, rather than non-British participants or participants of dual nationality.

limits: the countries of the non-British students are not given in the abstract
same scale as Mauss 2011 (Valuing Happiness Scale), whose structure is questioned (Luhmann 2016)
